title: 18-year-old uses ‘grit and determination’ to help with own rescue from Mount Washington
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Andrew Nelson, 18, from Topsfield, Massachusetts, sustained a leg injury while hiking on Mount Washington's Tuckerman Ravine Trail.
Nelson used hopping and crawling to move three-tenths of a mile towards the summit to meet rescuers.
Rescue crews applied a vacuum splint and transported him to the summit, but he declined hospital transport.

title: Woman sues Court TV over release of her name in Irish firefighter rape case
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Woman sues Court TV for $2.8 million, alleging it disclosed her identity during a retrial of an Irish firefighter accused of rape.
The lawsuit claims the network revealed her name twice on-screen and on social media, leading to widespread online harassment.
Court TV admitted accidental disclosure in court; a judge confirmed victim's identity was exposed before content was removed.

title: Healey signs sweeping law to restrict ICE
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed the Protect Act in Chelsea, restricting ICE actions in Massachusetts.
The law prohibits warrantless immigration arrests in schools, hospitals, and other sensitive locations.
The Protect Act expands legal protections for immigrants and introduces a state civil rights claim.

title: Here’s how Mass. hospitals fared in the latest U.S. News rankings
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Brigham and Women's Hospital and Massachusetts General Hospital tied for first in Massachusetts in latest U.S. News rankings.
Both hospitals, part of Mass General Brigham, were among 20 nationwide on the U.S. News hospital honor roll.
Dana-Farber Brigham Cancer Center ranked third in the U.S. for cancer care in the specialized care category.

title: Stefon Diggs reportedly ‘set to sign’ with Commanders on one-year deal
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Stefon Diggs is reportedly signing a one-year deal with the Washington Commanders, potentially worth up to $12 million.
Diggs helped the New England Patriots reach the Super Bowl in 2025, being their first 1,000-yard receiver since 2019.
Patriots parted ways with Diggs after acquiring receiver A.J. Brown; Diggs was previously found not guilty of assault charges.

title: Patriots teammates believe Will Campbell is ready for Year 2 jump
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Will Campbell, Patriots left tackle, shows improvement during training camp, impressing teammates like Dre’Mont Jones and Drake Maye.
Campbell faced challenges last season, notably recording 14 pressures in Super Bowl LX against the Seahawks.
The Patriots anticipate a major Year 2 improvement from Campbell, hoping to bolster their offensive line effectiveness.

title: Snag one-way fares for as low as $54 during JetBlue’s fall travel flash sale
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: JetBlue launched a 48-hour flash sale offering one-way fares as low as $54 for fall travel.
Sale ends Thursday at 11:59 p.m. EDT and covers travel on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Saturdays until Nov. 18.
Blackout dates include Oct. 9-14 and Nov. 8-11; fares available through jetblue.com.

title: Moulton doubles down on Epstein-related attacks on Markey
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Rep. Seth Moulton accuses Sen. Ed Markey of ties to Jeffrey Epstein, citing newly-released files during a debate.
Moulton alleged Markey had ties to a lobbyist representing Epstein, though Markey denies ever meeting the notorious financier.
Moulton's campaign is pressing for Markey to donate contributions linked to Epstein, though both received funds from the same lobbyist.

title: New Red Sox reliever Erik Miller says he learned about trade from TV
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Erik Miller learned about his trade to the Red Sox from a TV announcement before playing catch.
Miller made his Red Sox debut with a strikeout after traveling cross-country; he's adapting to Fenway Park.
Miller boosts the Red Sox bullpen with a 2.14 ERA over his last 75 outings across the 2025 and 2026 seasons.

title: ‘Sheer grit and determination’: Mass. 18-year-old with leg injury meets rescuers halfway on Mount Washington
author: John Waller
bullets: Andrew Nelson, 18, from Topsfield, Mass., was injured hiking on Mount Washington's Tuckerman Ravine Trail.
Nelson hiked 0.3 miles despite a leg injury using assistance from friends until rescuers arrived.
A vacuum splint was used on his leg; he was carried 0.2 miles before opting for treatment at home.
